Fold Change vs. Feature Metric Plot (MA-style)

Source: R/plot_fcmetric.R
plot_fcmetric.Rd

Plots the fold change of each feature (y-axis) against a per-feature metric (x-axis): mean abundance (the classic MA plot), effect size, variance, standard deviation, or VIP score. Unlike plot_volcano() it needs no p-values, so it remains useful when run_diff() found nothing significant. With metric = "abundance" it shows whether large fold changes come from low-intensity "noise" features whose baseline is near zero. Styling arguments match plot_volcano().

Usage

plot_fcmetric(
  x,
  y = NULL,
  z = NULL,
  group = NULL,
  features = NULL,
  metric = c("abundance", "effect_size", "variance", "sd", "vip"),
  log2 = TRUE,
  log10_x = NULL,
  x_cut = NULL,
  up = 1.5,
  down = 0.5,
  annotate = NULL,
  use_ggrepel = TRUE,
  up_color = "red",
  down_color = "blue",
  ns_color = "grey60",
  h_color = NULL,
  v_color = NULL,
  size = 5,
  alpha = 0.6,
  theme = "nature",
  plot_title = NULL,
  plot_subtitle = NULL,
  xlab = NULL,
  ylab = NULL,
  global_font_size = 25,
  title_size = NULL,
  subtitle_size = NULL,
  xlab_size = NULL,
  ylab_size = NULL,
  axis_text_size = NULL,
  label_size = NULL,
  legend_size = NULL,
  legend_title = NULL,
  legend_nrow = NULL,
  ...
)

Arguments

x

A run_foldchange() result, or a named list holding it plus the object needed by metric, e.g. list(fc = fc, diff = diff, pls = pls); or a data.frame/tibble/named matrix with one row per feature. One plot is made per comparison.

The data stage (normalized, transformed, scaled, ...) is chosen upstream, e.g. run_foldchange(from = "normalized"). For a data.frame, supply columns computed from whichever stage you want.

y

A single character string naming the column of raw fold changes (positive numeric). Default NULL ("fold_change" for run_foldchange() input).

z

A single character string naming the column holding the x-axis metric. Default NULL (derived from x and metric for run_foldchange() input; required for a data.frame, where metric then only sets the axis label and default scale).

group

An optional column name in x; one plot is made per level. Default NULL.

features

A single character string naming the feature identifier column. Required when annotate is used. Default NULL.

metric

A single string, the x-axis metric. See Metrics. Default "abundance".

log2

Logical. If TRUE (default) the y-axis is \(\log_2\)(fold change); if FALSE it is the raw fold change.

log10_x

Logical or NULL. If TRUE the x-axis is \(\log_{10}\) of the metric. Default NULL chooses automatically: TRUE for "abundance", "variance" and "sd"; FALSE for "effect_size" and "vip". If the metric has non-positive values it is set to FALSE with a warning.

x_cut

Optional numeric vector of reference values (on the original metric scale, not log10) drawn as vertical dashed lines, e.g. 1 for VIP or c(0.2, 0.5, 0.8) for Cohen's d. Default NULL.

up, down

Raw fold-change thresholds (up > 1, 0 < down < 1). Features beyond them are coloured Up/Down. Inherited from a run_foldchange() object when missing; otherwise 1.5/0.5.

annotate

Optional (named) character vector of feature identifiers to label; see plot_volcano. Default NULL.

use_ggrepel, up_color, down_color, ns_color, h_color, v_color, size, alpha, theme, plot_title, plot_subtitle, xlab, ylab, global_font_size, title_size, subtitle_size, xlab_size, ylab_size, axis_text_size, label_size, legend_size, legend_title, legend_nrow, ...

As in plot_volcano. Here h_color colours the horizontal up/down fold-change lines and v_color the vertical x_cut lines. plot_title = NULL gives a title naming the metric (plus the comparison when there are several).

Value

A list of class plot_fcmetric with plots (named list of ggplot objects), classified (data with the metric in metric_value and .regulation) and params.

Metrics

"abundance"

Mean of the two group means of each comparison. Needs only run_foldchange().

"variance", "sd"

Pooled within-group variance / SD of the two groups in each comparison, \(s_p^2 = ((n_1-1)s_1^2 + (n_2-1)s_2^2)/(n_1+n_2-2)\), on the same data scale as the fold change. Needs only run_foldchange(). Raw-intensity variance typically grows with abundance; consider transformed data for a variance-stabilised view.

"effect_size"

Per-feature estimate from run_diff() (multi-outcome; e.g. Cohen's d, rank-biserial, eta-squared depending on the test chosen). Supply list(fc = ..., diff = ...). The estimate is one value per feature, so with more than two groups it is omnibus and repeats across comparisons. Estimates from different effect-size metrics are not directly comparable; a warning is given when they are mixed.

"vip"

VIP score from run_pls() (PLS-DA/OPLS-DA; sPLS-DA yields none). Supply list(fc = ..., pls = ...). One value per feature, repeated across comparisons.

References

Cohen J (1988). Statistical Power Analysis for the Behavioral Sciences (2nd ed.). Lawrence Erlbaum Associates.

Wickham H (2016). ggplot2: Elegant Graphics for Data Analysis. Springer-Verlag New York. doi:10.1007/978-3-319-24277-4

See also

plot_volcano, run_foldchange, run_diff, run_pls

Author

John Lennon L. Calorio

Examples

x    <- iris[iris$Species != "setosa", 1:4]
meta <- droplevels(iris[iris$Species != "setosa", "Species", drop = FALSE])
fc   <- run_foldchange(x, metadata = meta, group = "Species")

plot_fcmetric(fc)                                  # MA-style plot
#> -- plot_fcmetric results -----------------------------------
#>   Metric     : abundance
#>   Features   : 4  (Up: 0 | Down: 0 | NS: 4)
#>   Thresholds : FC >= 1.5000 (up) | <= 0.5000 (down)
#>   Plots      : Fold Change vs. Mean Abundance
plot_fcmetric(fc, metric = "sd", global_font_size = 12)
#> -- plot_fcmetric results -----------------------------------
#>   Metric     : sd
#>   Features   : 4  (Up: 0 | Down: 0 | NS: 4)
#>   Thresholds : FC >= 1.5000 (up) | <= 0.5000 (down)
#>   Plots      : Fold Change vs. Standard Deviation

# \donttest{
dif <- run_diff(x, meta, outcome = names(x), group = "Species",
                summary_table = TRUE, verbose = FALSE)
plot_fcmetric(list(fc = fc, diff = dif), metric = "effect_size",
              x_cut = c(0.2, 0.5, 0.8))
#> Warning: Effect sizes use different metrics (Rank-biserial correlation, Cohen's d); they are not directly comparable.
#> -- plot_fcmetric results -----------------------------------
#>   Metric     : effect_size
#>   Features   : 4  (Up: 0 | Down: 0 | NS: 4)
#>   Thresholds : FC >= 1.5000 (up) | <= 0.5000 (down)
#>   Plots      : Fold Change vs. Effect Size
# }
